panels.title: Disks failing SMART

targets.expr: count(smartctl_device_smart_status == 0) or vector(0)

panels.description: Drives whose SMART overall-health self-assessment is FAILED. Replace immediately.

panels.title: SATA sector problems

targets.expr: sum(smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect"}) or vector(0)

panels.description: Sum of reallocated, pending, offline-uncorrectable and reported-uncorrectable sectors across all SATA drives. Any non-zero value is worth investigating; a rising value means a dying disk.

panels.title: SAS defects / uncorrected

targets.expr: (sum(smartctl_scsi_grown_defect_list) or vector(0)) + (sum(smartctl_read_total_uncorrected_errors) or vector(0)) + (sum(smartctl_write_total_uncorrected_errors) or vector(0))

panels.description: Grown defect list + uncorrected read/write errors across SAS drives (disk3, parity1). SAS drives don't report ATA attributes; these are their equivalent.

panels.title: Hottest disk

targets.expr: max(smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"})

panels.description: Highest current drive temperature. HDDs are happiest under ~45°C.

panels.title: Since last SnapRAID sync

targets.expr: time() - snapraid_last_sync_success_timestamp_seconds

panels.description: Time since snapraid-nightly.sh last completed a successful sync. Over 48h means syncs are failing or being aborted (check logs/snapraid-*.log).

panels.title: Last SnapRAID run

targets.expr: snapraid_sync_aborted * 2 + (snapraid_sync_exit_code != bool 0)

panels.description: Outcome of the most recent nightly run. ABORTED means the mass-deletion safety check refused to sync: run 'snapraid diff' / 'snapraid status' before syncing by hand.

panels.title: Disks

targets.expr: (smartctl_device) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")
smartctl_device_smart_status
smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"}
smartctl_device_power_on_seconds
smartctl_device_capacity_bytes

max by (device) (label_replace(1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+"))

panels.description: One row per physical disk. Device letters (sdX) can change after a reboot; Mount and Serial don't.

panels.title: Filesystem usage

targets.expr: 1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes

panels.description: Per-disk and pool usage. mergerfs stops placing new files on a branch at minfreespace (200G).

panels.title: Drive temperature

targets.expr: (smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"}) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"}, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Current temperature per drive. Sustained >45°C shortens HDD life; a single drive running much hotter than its neighbours usually means an airflow problem in that bay.

panels.title: SATA drives (disk1, disk2, OS SSD, unmounted WDs)
Critical SATA attributes (raw values)

targets.expr: label_join((smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect|UDMA_CRC_Error_Count"}) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect|UDMA_CRC_Error_Count"}, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", ""), "disk", " ", "mountpoint", "device")

panels.description: The attributes that best predict failure. Should all be 0. Reallocated = sectors already swapped for spares; Pending = unreadable sectors awaiting reallocation; UDMA CRC = cable/backplane errors, not the disk itself.

panels.title: Sector problems over time

targets.expr: (smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect"}) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name=~"Reallocated_Sector_Ct|Current_Pending_Sector|Offline_Uncorrectable|Reported_Uncorrect"}, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Trend matters more than the number: a count that keeps climbing means the disk is failing.

panels.title: UDMA CRC errors (cabling)

targets.expr: (smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name="UDMA_CRC_Error_Count"}) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_attribute{attribute_value_type="raw", attribute_name="UDMA_CRC_Error_Count"}, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Increases point at a bad SATA cable, breakout cable or backplane slot, not the disk.

panels.title: Power-on hours

targets.expr: (smartctl_device_power_on_seconds / 3600) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_power_on_seconds / 3600, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Drive age. Annual failure rates climb noticeably after ~5 years (~44k hours).

panels.title: Grown defects

targets.expr: (smartctl_scsi_grown_defect_list) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_scsi_grown_defect_list, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Sectors the drive has remapped since leaving the factory (the SAS equivalent of Reallocated_Sector_Ct). A few is OK if stable; any growth is a warning sign.

panels.title: Uncorrected read errors

targets.expr: (smartctl_read_total_uncorrected_errors) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_read_total_uncorrected_errors, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Reads the drive could not recover even with ECC and retries. Should be 0.

panels.title: Uncorrected write errors

targets.expr: (smartctl_write_total_uncorrected_errors) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_write_total_uncorrected_errors, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Writes the drive could not complete. Should be 0.

panels.title: Temperature vs. drive trip point

targets.expr: (smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"} / on(device) smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="drive_trip"}) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="current"} / on(device) smartctl_device_temperature{temperature_type="drive_trip"}, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: SAS drives report the temperature at which they protect themselves (60°C here). Shown as % of that trip point.

panels.title: Grown defect list over time

targets.expr: (smartctl_scsi_grown_defect_list) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smartctl_scsi_grown_defect_list, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Should be a flat line. Steps up mean the platters are degrading.

panels.title: ECC-corrected errors per day

targets.expr: (increase(smartctl_read_errors_corrected_by_eccdelayed[1d])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(increase(smartctl_read_errors_corrected_by_eccdelayed[1d]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

(increase(smartctl_write_errors_corrected_by_eccdelayed[1d])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(increase(smartctl_write_errors_corrected_by_eccdelayed[1d]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

(increase(smartctl_read_errors_corrected_by_rereads_rewrites[1d])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(increase(smartctl_read_errors_corrected_by_rereads_rewrites[1d]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

(increase(smartctl_write_errors_corrected_by_rereads_rewrites[1d])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(increase(smartctl_write_errors_corrected_by_rereads_rewrites[1d]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Errors the drive recovered from, but only with extra effort (delayed ECC or retries). Fast ECC corrections are normal and omitted. A rising trend here often precedes grown defects.

panels.title: SMART self-test results
panels.description: From each drive's own self-test log (scripts/smart-selftest-metrics.sh, hourly). Short tests run Saturdays; each drive gets a long test once a month (schedule in maintenance-notes.md). Ages count power-on time. A long test older than ~45 days means one was missed or aborted. 'Failed in log' counts failures among the last ~20 tests the drive remembers.

targets.expr: (smart_selftest_last_long_status) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smart_selftest_last_long_status, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")
smart_selftest_last_long_age_seconds
smart_selftest_last_short_status
smart_selftest_last_short_age_seconds
smart_selftest_failed
smart_selftest_running

panels.title: Failed self-tests over time
panels.description: Failed tests in each drive's self-test log. One failure is a data point; a count that keeps climbing month after month means plan a replacement. Compare with 'Sector problems over time' and 'Grown defect list over time'.

targets.expr: (smart_selftest_failed) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(smart_selftest_failed, "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.title: Throughput

targets.expr: (rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

(-rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(-rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Reads above zero, writes below. Expect parity1 to be busy only during the nightly sync.

panels.title: Busy time

targets.expr: (rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) group by (device, mountpoint) (label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/sd[a-z]+[0-9]+", mountpoint=~"/mnt/[^/]+|/"}, "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+)[0-9]+")) or on(device) label_replace(rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total{device=~"sd[a-z]+"}[$__rate_interval]), "mountpoint", "unmounted", "", "")

panels.description: Fraction of time each disk had I/O in flight. Near 100% = that disk is the bottleneck.
